composition.observation: The open parchment Journal remains the main reading object. Connecting a phone places a bounded dark dialog over that same book, with a large QR square and a clear close affordance; it reads as a temporary task within the Voyage.

hierarchy.observation: Connect another device is quiet within the Journal tools. Once opened, the phone instruction and QR lead, with account and code guidance below; Continue the Chronicle provides a clear end to the task without competing with the code.

typography.observation: The serif passage title and comfortably spaced body remain readable on parchment. The connection panel switches to concise interface text, preserving distinct heading, instruction, account note and code levels on both widths.

spacing.observation: Desktop gives the QR generous breathing room and separates the recovery/code alternative. At 390 pixels the panel becomes a vertically scrollable column; its text and actions stay within the frame rather than compressing into the Journal beneath.

controls.observation: The contextual Connect control opens the actual phone setup. Close and Continue the Chronicle dismiss it, and the readable Journal is available again. QR scanning and completing a second device connection were not exercised by this single-context journey.

contrast.observation: Cream instructions, brass emphasis and dark teal give the connection panel a readable hierarchy; the high contrast black and white QR is visually distinct. The returned objective and Continue Voyage remain legible against the gold panel.

consistency.observation: The brass, sea-green, serif and parchment language is consistent with the accepted Homeport reference family and the underlying Journal. The dialog preserves the current Voyage rather than introducing a differently branded device dashboard.

states.observation: The sequence shows an active passage, a ready QR/code task with account and expiry guidance, and a restored passage. These are useful rendered states; a receiving phone, a successful pairing acknowledgement and a revoked connection are outside this sequence.

responsive.observation: The desktop book and dialog fit a broad reading surface. On the narrow viewport the tool area wraps and the phone setup scrolls vertically; the fixed objective remains below the passage and Continue Voyage is not covered by the four Journal tabs.

keyboard.observation: The trace records Tab traversal and Enter activation through the connection task and safe return in all four contexts. The recording shows the resulting modal and returned book, so the keyboard path changes the real task rather than only locating controls.

focus.observation: Visible outlines identify the active Journal tool and modal controls. After the reduced-motion phone dialog closes, focus returns to the Connect trigger; the normal phone ending is scrolled lower but still returns to the Journal rather than trapping focus in the dismissed panel.

feedback.observation: Opening the dialog yields a usable QR and instructions promptly, and closing it restores the passage without a second task screen. Producer activation-to-outcome measurements span about 227 to 412 ms; the complete timelines show no unresolved waiting state at the outcome.

motion.observation: Normal playback includes the Journal opening settling into its stated readable fallback before connection. Reduced motion exposes the same tools, QR and return without needing a ceremony. The modal transition itself does not require motion to explain what changed.

continuity.observation: Before opening, inside the contextual task and after dismissal, the experience remains attached to Synthetic Crossdeck refit Voyage and the same passage. Original continuity witnesses retain the Voyage and edition. This proves local context preservation, not a two-context pairing or acknowledged handoff.

complexity.observation: The Player encounters one contextual connection task, with scanning first and a code alternative when needed. The Journal does not expose a device inventory or require the Player to interpret transport state to resume reading.

role-outcomes.observation: The authorized Player can open private phone guidance from Follow the lanterns and return directly to that reading task. The QR is a real rendered connection artifact, but no evidence here warrants claiming that a second phone joined or took over the Voyage.

fallbacks.observation: The dialog offers an account-aware connection instruction and a code route alongside QR scanning, while close and Continue the Chronicle preserve a conventional exit. Journal motion failure is plainly disclosed and leaves page reading and the contextual connection usable.

findings.observation: A contextual, QR-led phone task preserves the readable active Journal and provides code guidance and direct close/Continue exits on desktop and phone. The captured single-context boundary is explicit; actual remote pairing is not accepted by this review.

composition.observation: A persistent Voyage header and compact status line frame one substantial purpose panel. The Lens clue, chart, full passage and artifact each occupy that panel as content, rather than becoming a set of equal dashboard tiles.

hierarchy.observation: Voyage identity and Return to Chronicle sit above the current purpose. Within the purpose panel the heading leads to the released content; Change purpose and its Continue action form a secondary choice task, with additional purposes disclosed separately.

typography.observation: The Journal companion presents the complete passage in a narrow serif reading column, and A/A+ visibly changes reading size. Chart labels and artifact description remain readable interface/content layers rather than replacing prose with role names.

spacing.observation: Purpose content has its own padded panel and bounded text width. The narrow artifact view preserves space around the titled card and description while using ordinary vertical scrolling; the reading-size controls remain separate from the artifact image.

controls.observation: Keyboard choices open the actual Lens, chart and artifact outcomes and restore Journal. A/A+ is a real reading aid. Return to Chronicle leads to the same Journal, while Exit to My Voyages offers an understandable broader context exit.

contrast.observation: The cream content, muted green status and brass accents remain clear on dark teal; the artifact and passage use dark ink on parchment. The current purpose heading has a conspicuous light focus outline on the narrow view.

consistency.observation: All four purposes retain the same Voyage header, status, return vocabulary and restrained Homeport materials. Their content layouts change to suit reading, map or artifact inspection without making each purpose feel like a separate application.

states.observation: Each named state contains a useful result: the Captain note in Guided Lens, an authored chart and Secret Isle objective, the full Follow the lanterns passage, and The brass compass with its released description. Journal restoration follows the purpose changes.

responsive.observation: At phone width the Voyage identity, full-width return link and single purpose panel stack cleanly. Long artifact content continues below the fold with readable wrapping, and the complete phone timeline shows purpose selection and return remaining available.

keyboard.observation: The recorded Tab/Enter sequence reaches the purpose chooser, actual purpose transitions, reading controls and return. All four traces contain 12 Enter activations and a complete sequence of useful rendered purpose outcomes; this exceeds a role-label existence check.

focus.observation: After changing purpose, the purpose heading receives a clearly visible outline, allowing the new workspace to be found immediately. Lens owns modal focus while open, and returning to the Journal restores a conventional reading context.

feedback.observation: The purpose selection produces its named content promptly, and the status settles to Same Voyage - in sync. Brief reconnecting observations in the setup timeline and event-stream rate limits are real, but the captured outcomes recover instead of leaving empty purpose panels; measured transition feedback is about 90 to 142 ms.

motion.observation: Purpose changes are direct and readable in normal and reduced motion. Neither chart nor artifact discovery depends on animation; the returning Journal can use its disclosed readable opening fallback while retaining the passage and controls.

continuity.observation: The purpose changes retain Synthetic Crossdeck refit Voyage and the same immutable edition, then return to its Journal. The content corresponds to that Voyage rather than a generic purpose demonstration. In-sync presentation in one context does not establish cross-device transfer or remote acknowledgement.

complexity.observation: The purpose chooser keeps the core Lens, Chart and Journal choices together and puts the extra artifact purpose behind More purposes. The Player chooses a use for the screen rather than configuring rendering providers or connection transport.

role-outcomes.observation: The Player can read the full released passage, see the actual sparse chart and its Secret Isle objective, inspect the released Captain note, and read the brass compass description. The artifact illustration is a simple star-bearing parchment card, but the titled object and description carry specific authored meaning.

fallbacks.observation: Guided Lens supplies the released clue with camera off, and the Journal remains a conventional readable purpose with a direct return. The recording does not demonstrate a native camera or every unavailable-purpose branch, so those capabilities receive no broader acceptance here.

findings.observation: The four purposes provide released, Voyage-specific reading, clue, chart and artifact outcomes within a consistent companion frame. The chart is sparse but authored, and the artifact has a specific title and description; neither is only a role label.

composition.observation: Lens is a bounded foreground workspace over the active Journal. Its parchment clue object, title and guided-view explanation give the spatial content a readable home without obscuring where the Player can close it.

hierarchy.observation: The Captain note and its clue text lead the Lens experience, followed by the Inspect interaction and its response. Guided view is explicit, while camera-related capability remains secondary to reading the published clue.

typography.observation: The title, quoted clue and entity description are legible at both widths. The inspection message names the Captain note and its parchment description, so the response is understandable prose rather than a technical event token.

spacing.observation: Desktop separates the scene, clue reading and action area; phone width stacks them in a scrollable dialog with enough internal spacing to distinguish the object from status and controls. Closing preserves Journal scroll position. At the lower desktop return, the right-edge Journal tabs crowd and partly overlap the far-right edge of Open Chronicle Lens; the action remains readable and operable, but more horizontal clearance would improve polish.

controls.observation: Open Lens, Inspect and Close perform visible actions. Inspect adds entity-specific feedback and an interaction-recorded response; Close removes the dialog, and the timeline shows that the same Lens can be reopened. This does not demonstrate canonical passage advancement.

contrast.observation: The parchment clue uses dark ink, while the surrounding dark workspace uses cream labels and brass action emphasis. Both the initial clue and the inspection feedback stay readable without relying on the scene alone.

consistency.observation: Lens shares the Journal and Homeport serif, parchment and brass language. Its Close action and the restored Open Lens control use the same contextual vocabulary, so the published clue feels attached to the current Chronicle.

states.observation: Ready and inspected states differ in meaningful content: the actual northern-light clue is readable first, then the Captain note receives a named inspection response and recorded-interaction notice. The returned state is the Journal, not an empty success page.

responsive.observation: The phone Lens remains a readable single column with a reachable close control and clue interaction. The restored phone objective and Continue Voyage remain visible below the book; the dialog does not leave a covering overlay behind.

keyboard.observation: All four traces show Tab traversal, opening, inspection and closing through Enter. The visible clue and added response corroborate that keyboard input reached the published object interaction rather than merely focusing a hidden action.

focus.observation: The Lens modal establishes a contained task, and closing returns focus to the visible Open Lens control. The desktop return looks sparse at its lower scroll position, but full-resolution reading shows the preceding passage above; the control and position survive.

feedback.observation: Inspect visibly adds You are inspecting the Captain note and the recorded-interaction explanation. The useful outcome appears within the complete timelines; producer transition measurements of about 143 to 291 ms support the absence of a long unresolved wait, without proving a remote consumer acknowledgement.

motion.observation: The clue and feedback remain intelligible without animated scene exploration. Both motion modes reach the same inspected and returned states; normal Journal opening may use the disclosed readable fallback, which does not prevent Lens use.

continuity.observation: The published Captain note is opened from Follow the lanterns, inspected and closed within the same named Voyage and edition. The preserved Journal and focus show local continuity; a recorded clue interaction is not evidence that the Voyage has advanced to another passage.

complexity.observation: The task is small and coherent: open the released clue, read it, inspect the named object and close. The guided mode keeps camera permission from becoming a prerequisite to understanding the clue.

role-outcomes.observation: The Player reads the actual published clue, The next bearing is written in the stars, with a direction to look for the northern light. Inspect yields an entity-specific response tied to the Captain note. This is meaningful released content, with authoring/publication itself outside this consumer review.
